item.title: Judge Orders Return of Slavery Exhibit at President’s House, Barbican Director Devyani Saltzman Departs: Morning Links for February 17, 2026
item.description: Here's what we're reading this morning, folks.

item.title: Paul Slocum, One of Digital Art’s First Champions, on Building a Sustainable Digital Ecosystem
item.description: This past week, Paul Slocum celebrated 20 years of And/Or gallery, a pioneering space for the exhibition of new media art.

item.title: British Museum Contests Report on Removal of ‘Palestinian’ from Some Wall Texts
item.description: The museum distanced itself from a pro-Israel group that claimed it played a role in the decision.

item.title: University of North Texas Faculty Calls on School to Disclose Reason for Cancelation of Victor Quiñonez Exhibition
item.description: “The removal of legally protected artistic expression from a university gallery contradicts the institution’s own commitments to academic freedom, constitutional principles, and the open exchange of ideas fundamental to higher education,” the letter reads.

item.title: Eugenio Viola Says Museo de Arte Moderno de Bogotá Ended His Contract Over Labor Issues
item.description: Viola is claiming that the board of directors did so after he raised concerns with working conditions at the museum.

item.title: Macron Adviser Anne-Claire Legendre Tapped to Head Institut du Monde Arabe
item.description: Her appointment signals a desire for renewal at an institution that has struggled in recent years.

item.title: Citing George Orwell, Federal Judge Orders Reinstatement of Slavery Display at George Washington’s Presidential House
item.description: The displays referring to Washington's ownership of enslaved people were removed by the Trump administration.

item.title: Australian Police Catch Thief Behind Heist of Egyptian Artifacts
item.description: Police discovered part of the stolen haul in a camper van, including a 2,600-year-old wooden cat figure from Egypt’s 26th Dynasty.

item.title: Artist Trevor Paglen Thinks Steven Spielberg’s Disclosure Day Looks Awfully Familiar
item.description: Paglen took to Instagram to note the link between his 2024 and 2025 shows, which explored the history of UFO photography, and the new Spielberg film.

item.title: More than 100 Cuban Cultural Leaders Call for International Aid in Face of Oil Blockade
item.description: In a public letter, Cuban artists and writers criticize the longstanding U.S. economic embargo for causing a humanitarian crisis.
